title: Cascading SLO Failure Mitigation and Federated Budget Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a federated SLO budget model and an operational runbook to detect, contain, and recover from cascading SLO failures across the Redwood inference stack (edge proxy, routing, serving runtime, and storage/KV subsystems). It prescribes an automated credit-leasing protocol, priority-driven request shaping, and manual escalation steps to preserve critical SLAs while minimizing customer impact and cost.

Scope:
- Applies to: edge-proxy, request-router, runtime-allocator, kv-cache, model-serving pool (hosted and dedicated), and routing fallback orchestrator.
- Not in scope: billing reconciliation, model training pipelines, and customer-managed on-prem control planes (except where telemetry proxies route to Redwood control plane).

Motivation:
Cascading failures often occur when one subsystem exhausts its capacity and backpressure is incorrectly propagated or unbounded. We need a bounded, auditable mechanism to reallocate limited SLO budget across services and tenants in a predictable way and an operational checklist for engineers and on-call to act quickly.

Definitions:
- Federated SLO Budget: a per-service pool of SLO 'credits' (latency/error allowances) that can be temporarily leased to dependent services during transient pressure.
- Credit Lease: a time-bound transfer of budget from one service's pool to another with automatic repayment rules.
- Priority Lane: a request classification (critical/standard/batch) used to drive admission control and shaping.
- Degradation Fence: pre-approved behavior that reduces fidelity (quantization, token limit, sampling) for non-critical traffic.

Design Principles:
- Predictability: leases are capped, time-limited, and compensated in repayment windows to avoid permanent budget erosion.
- Observability-first: every lease, shape, and eviction emits typed telemetry and audit events.
- SLO-first: preserve high-priority SLOs (customer-tiered) over low-priority workloads by design.
- Minimal blast radius: prefer localized degradation and fallback over global throttles.

Federated Budget Model (overview):
- Each service S has: capacity_estimate, credit_pool (units = percentage of SLO budget), committed_reservations, and outstanding_leases.
- Default allocations: edge-proxy 25%, routing 20%, runtime-allocator 35%, kv-cache 20% (tunable per environment).
- Credit unit: 1 credit = 0.01% of service-level 99th percentile latency budget or 0.01% error budget (mutually exclusive depending on event type).

Credit Leasing Protocol (sequence):
1) Detection: service B (downstream) emits SLO-stress alert when its 99p latency exceeds threshold T1 for 3 consecutive 30s windows or error-rate exceeds E1 for 2 consecutive 1m windows.
2) Pre-check: B queries local credit_pool and outstanding_leases. If insufficient, B sends LeaseRequest to upstream candidate L (routing/runtime-allocator/edge-proxy) with: {service_id, requested_credits, lease_ttl_seconds, priority_lane}.
3) Decision: L evaluates local credit_pool and current commitments using policy rules (min_reserve, max_lease_fraction, tenant_fairness_delta). If accept: L emits LeaseGranted event and decrements its credit_pool; otherwise LeaseDenied.
4) Enforcement: If LeaseGranted, B enters a soft-expansion mode for TTL where it relaxes non-critical admission control up to leased capacity and emits audit records.
5) Repayment: After TTL or once B recovers, B must emit LeaseRelease indicating actual_usage. If actual_usage < granted, difference is returned. If usage > granted, Governance action (see Enforcement rules) triggers: either forced repayment from next reward window or initiating a cascading degrade on low-priority lanes.

Policy knobs (defaults):
- max_lease_fraction_per_service = 0.2 (no service gives away >20% of its pool at a time).
- min_reserve = 0.15 (must keep 15% to preserve local safety headroom).
- lease_ttl_default = 120 (seconds).
- acceptance_latency_margin = 1.2 (only grant if current latency < 1.2 * SLO_target).
- priority_preference_order = [critical, standard, batch].

Automated Mitigations and Fencing:
- Priority admission: when combined outstanding_leases exceed threshold, runtime-allocator drops or delays batch lane requests first, then standard. Critical lane always allowed unless catastrophic exhaustion.
- Degradation profiles (pre-approved):
  - Batch: pause, reroute to dedicated cold capacity, or convert to background job.
  - Standard: reduce max_tokens by 50%, enable aggressive prefix/KV cache reuse, lower generation temperature to reduce token churn.
  - Critical: enable model-variant fallback (quantized smaller variant) and burst ticketing.
- Fallback routing: edge-proxy can direct requests to model-variant or alternate region if lease fails but routing policy allows (cost implications logged).

Observability signals (must be instrumented):
- slo.latency.99p per service and per priority_lane (gauge/time series)
- slo.error_rate.1m per service and per priority_lane
- federation.lease.requests, federation.lease.granted, federation.lease.denied (counters)
- federation.lease.outstanding_bytes (gauge)
- admission.drop.count by cause and lane (counter)
- audit.event for every Lease* action (structured log with lease_id, giver, taker, ttl, reason)
- tenant-impact.score (derived signal used for post-incident analysis)

Alert thresholds (example):
- T1 latency stress: 99p > 1.5 * SLO_target for 90s -> SLO-STRESS alert
- E1 error stress: 1m error_rate > 1.0% absolute or 3x baseline for 2 consecutive minutes -> ERROR-STRESS alert
- Lease saturation: federation.lease.outstanding_bytes > 80% of global federated_pool -> FED_POOL_ALMOST_FULL

Runbook: immediate steps for on-call (ordered):
1) Acknowledge SLO-STRESS alert and open incident channel.
2) Run quick blast-radius query: identify which services and priority lanes are affected (use prebuilt dashboards).
3) If downstream has LeaseRequest inflight: verify LeaseGranted events and audit trail. If none, consider manual LeaseGrant from candidate service owner within policy knobs.
4) If federated pool is saturated: flip federation-mode to "conservative" (automated flag) which reduces max_lease_fraction_per_service to 0.05 and forces immediate degradation on batch lane.
5) If tenant-specific impact: apply tenant-scoped admission limits (rate-limits) to offending tenant(s) as measured by tenant-impact.score > 0.7.
6) If automated mitigations fail after 5 minutes: escalate to Runtime/SRE lead and open a hotfix channel. Consider temporary capacity burst (if available) or region-level routing fallback.
7) After recovery: submit post-incident events (see Post-Incident checklist).

Post-Incident checklist (owner SRE oncall -> incident owner):
- Collect lease audit logs and correlate with SLO telemetry for affected windows.
- Compute repayment delta and reconcile credit pools.
- Run tenant impact analysis and notify customers if their SLA was affected (per customer communication policy).
- Create an incident timeline and tag relevant release/rollback IDs.
- Propose one of: increase capacity, adjust min_reserve, or refine acceptance_latency_margin depending on root cause.

Operationalization and rollout plan:
1) Implement telemetry hooks (federation.* metrics and Audit events) behind a feature flag in staging.
2) Run 2 game-days with synthetic pressure: a) kv-cache write storm; b) sudden model-variant cold-start. Validate lease flows and repayment.
3) Gradual rollout to prod: 10% traffic (canary) -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on FED_POOL_ALMOST_FULL or abnormal admission.drop spikes.
4) Governance: quarterly review of default allocations and max_lease_fraction with product and platform leads.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- SRE: own runbook, alerts, and game-days.
- Runtime team: implement enforcement, admission control, and audit logging.
- Edge/Proxy team: implement outbound LeaseRequest/acceptance and routing fallback.
- Observability: add dashboards and ensure retention for audit events (180 days).

Security and compliance notes:
- Lease audit events may contain tenant identifiers; ensure PII redaction where required and only store identifiers as hashed IDs for public dashboards.
- Any manual LeaseGrant must be recorded in the ticketing system and reference the lease_id.

Sample configuration table (YAML-like for illustration):
- federation_global_pool: 100000 (credits)
- service_allocations:
  - edge-proxy: 25000
  - routing: 20000
  - runtime-allocator: 35000
  - kv-cache: 20000
- policy:
  - max_lease_fraction_per_service: 0.2
  - min_reserve: 0.15
  - lease_ttl_default: 120
  - acceptance_latency_margin: 1.2

Example CLI snippets:
- Query outstanding leases: rdctl federation leases list --service runtime-allocator --window 10m
- Manually grant a lease (for emergencies only): rdctl federation leases grant --from routing --to runtime-allocator --credits 5000 --ttl 60 --reason "emergency kv write storm"

Decision record summary (why we chose leasing vs global throttles):
- Alternatives considered: global throttle, static preemption, and tenant-level pre-emptive throttles.
- Rationale: leasing gives bounded and auditable short-term flexibility, lowers unintended collateral damage, and can be tuned without cold starts. It also preserves the ability to make targeted post-incident compensations.

Open questions / backlog:
- How to integrate with Dedicated tenant capacity contracts (reserved capacity) for accurate credit accounting? (Action: runtime & billing team to define mapping by Q2 2025.)
- Should repayment be monetized (billing credit) or purely operational? (Action: finance & product to advise.)

Related artifacts and links:
- Implementation RFC (runtime team): confluence://eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/federation-rfc-2024
- Game-day plan & synthetic harness: confluence://eng-sre/game-days/federated-slo-gameday-2025

Appendix: quick math example
- Service A (routing) pool = 20k credits. A receives LeaseRequest of 4k credits (20%). Policy allows max_lease_fraction_per_service = 0.2. LeaseGranted for 120s.
- If B uses 3k only: 1k returned. If B uses 6k (overrun): enforcement will trigger degradation on B's low-priority lanes and record repayment due; if not paid, next compliance window reduces B's credit_pool by 5% for 24h.

Contact and escalation roster:
- Primary SRE oncall: see team rota (sre-oncall@redwood.ai)
- Runtime pager: runtime-pager@redwood.ai
- Edge/Proxy owner: alice.klein@redwood.ai

End of playbook.
